title: Self-Deception
coreMove: Separate felt sincerity from full self-knowledge, then ask what social signal the ignorance protects.
sourcePressure: The source presents self-deception as more than inner comfort: hidden truths can be kept from the self to make outward signals more convincing.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer turns self-deception into therapy talk or conscious lying with a nicer label.

sourceAnchors.name: older defensive theories versus newer evolutionary theories
sourceAnchors.detail: The source compares defensive theories of self-deception with evolutionary accounts of social advantage.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Comfort may be one benefit, but the cleaner public signal is another.

sourceAnchors.name: modular minds
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says modular minds allow inconsistent inner processes without one transparent center.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A divided mind can keep one room dark while another room speaks brightly.

sourceAnchors.name: self-discretion inside the mind
sourceAnchors.detail: The source names self-discretion as a way self-ignorance can become socially useful.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Not every part of the mind needs the same file before the face looks sincere.

exampleSpecs.audience: a curator defending a purchase that boosts her reputation
exampleSpecs.stakes: the acquisition may be sincere and self-serving at once
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia rereads her own memo beside the crate label and underlines every quality claim that also makes her look daring to trustees.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Pine crate splinters catch on Olivia's sleeve outside the loading bay.
mustAvoid: art chapter overlap about value signaling

exampleSpecs.audience: an organizer who believes she is rewarding dedication
exampleSpecs.stakes: table placement may hide a status alliance from the organizer herself
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Antoine earned that table," Frida says, then checks whether earned means volunteered most or flatters the donor she wants next year.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Antoine earned that table," Frida says while holding the seating cards.

exampleSpecs.audience: an attending convinced his praise is purely merit-based
exampleSpecs.stakes: a letter can protect a favored trainee while feeling honest
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took David one rejected resident to notice that his strongest adjectives followed loyalty more than skill, so he compares letters against case logs.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took David one rejected resident to reread the adjectives.

exampleSpecs.audience: a founder explaining an unequal split as fairness
exampleSpecs.stakes: the explanation may conceal fear of losing control
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You ask Lin to write the fairness reasons before and after seeing the cap table, exposing which reasons appear only when control is threatened.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see the cap table projected too large on the conference wall.

exampleSpecs.audience: a parent insisting the decision is only about academics
exampleSpecs.stakes: status anxiety may hide behind sincere concern
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Catarina places test scores and commute notes beside the private-school brochure and notices which facts she stops mentioning around other parents.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The private-school brochure sits brighter than the bus timetable.

exampleSpecs.audience: a committee member believing he is objective
exampleSpecs.stakes: the favored nominee strengthens the member's own faction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Which nominee looks most excellent after the faction map is covered?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which name remains at the top when the faction colors disappear?

skillTargets: identify when self-ignorance improves social signaling
use modular-mind logic without inventing clinical claims

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one confident explanation you gave this week. Add one sentence beginning, "This also makes me look..." and see what motive appears.
